question: At the mouth of which of the following rivers is the 'bird's foot' type delta formed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mississippi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mississippi river forms a **bird-foot delta**.
 
• It flows in the USA. It emerges from **Lake Itasca** in Minnesota.
 
• It flows into the **Gulf of Mexico**.
 
• It is the world's fourth longest river system including Missouri and Jefferson rivers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delta** is a depositional feature of a river.
 
• It is an important part of the **lower course of the river**.
 
• **Types of delta-**
 
 
• Arcuate Delta- It is a fan-shaped delta-like Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.
 
• Bird's foot delta - Its shape is like a bird's foot and hence the name. They are formed due to the deposition of finer materials by river water. Eg., Mississippi Delta
 
• Cuspate delta - When sediments are deposited in a straight line.
 
 
 
• **Other features of the river-**
 
 
• Upper course
 
 
• Gorges
 
• Waterfalls
 
• Rapids
 
 
 
• Middle course
